16, 22 tug₂ niĝ₂ mu₄-mu₄-bi; tug₂-ga mu₄-mu₄-bi nu-mu-un-zu-uš-am₃ בגד – דבר ללבוש – לא היה; בגד – את לבישתו לא ידעו וַיַּעַשׂ יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים לְאָדָם וּלְאִשְׁתּוֹ כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר וַיַּלְבִּשֵׁם (בראשית ג:כא) [divergence] The garment (tug₂ = בגד, mu₄ = לבש) is a cultural good brought by the gods with sheep and grain; in Gen 3:21 a garment of skin made by God after the sin.
107–111 tug₂ siki; um-ma-da-an-mur₁₀-re בגדי מצמר … אחרי שאותי לבשו כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר (בראשית ג:כא) [divergence] The sheep clothes king, gods and priests (wool, not skin).
40–42 du₆ kug-ta … ed₃ מן התל הטהור – נורידן; … מורידים וַיְשַׁלְּחֵהוּ יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים מִגַּן עֵדֶן לַעֲבֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה (בראשית ג:כג) [divergence] Inversion: the goods descend from the gods' place to man as a gift; in Genesis man is sent out of God's garden to till the ground.
27 mu-un-se₁₂-eš שָׁכְנוּ? וַיַּשְׁכֵּן מִקֶּדֶם לְגַן עֵדֶן אֶת הַכְּרֻבִים (בראשית ג:כד) [equivalent] Hebrew-only link (שכן); weak.
46 {ĝiš}apin šudul erin₂-bi מחרשה, עול וצמדו וְקַיִן הָיָה עֹבֵד אֲדָמָה (בראשית ד:ב) [equivalent] The farmer's tools are given by the gods; Genesis names no tool.
48, 125 sipad; na-gada; engar רועה; נוקד; איכר וַיְהִי הֶבֶל רֹעֵה צֹאן וְקַיִן הָיָה עֹבֵד אֲדָמָה (בראשית ד:ב) [equivalent] The two products of Gen 4:2 as two sisters: shepherd's product (Sheep) vs. farmer's product (Grain). engar > Akk. ikkaru > Heb. אִכָּר and na-gada = Akk. nāqidu = Heb. נֹקֵד are [cognate] loanwords.
72 nin₉ dub-saĝ-zu-me-en אחות, הראשונה שלך אני וַתֹּסֶף לָלֶדֶת אֶת אָחִיו אֶת הָבֶל (בראשית ד:ב) [divergence] Both claim precedence; in Genesis the farmer is the firstborn.
77 kadra {d}a-nun-na-ke₄-ne-me-en תשורת האנונה אני וַיָּבֵא קַיִן מִפְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה מִנְחָה לַיהוָה (בראשית ד:ג) [divergence] Grain as gift: of the gods to man here, of man to God there. מנחה deliberately not used for kadra.
105, 121 i₃ dug₃-ga; maš₂ … udu-utua₂ … mu-un-til-le-eš שמן טוב; גדייך … אילי־ההרבעה … תמו וְהֶבֶל הֵבִיא גַם הוּא מִבְּכֹרוֹת צֹאנוֹ וּמֵחֶלְבֵהֶן (בראשית ד:ד) [equivalent] Fat/oil (i₃ includes animal fat) and slaughtered rams and goats: the shepherd's offering. Our proposal (for i₃).
184, 193 2(MAN)-na-ne-ne {d}ezina₂ [ḫe₂-X]-gu-ul; u₈ taka₄-a {d}ezina₂ e₃-a משתיהן – דגן גדולה [תהיה]; כבשה – נותרת מאחור; דגן – יוצאת וַיִּשַׁע יְהוָה אֶל הֶבֶל וְאֶל מִנְחָתוֹ. וְאֶל קַיִן וְאֶל מִנְחָתוֹ לֹא שָׁעָה (בראשית ד:ד–ה) [divergence] The verdict is the reverse of Genesis: the god prefers the farmer's product; in Gen 4:4–5 God regards the shepherd's offering. In Dumuzid and Enkimdu (ETCSL 4.08.33) the shepherd wins, as in Genesis.
123 sipad-zu niĝ₂-ĝu₁₀-še₃ … igi-bi im-ši-ĝal₂ רועך … עינו אל אשר לי וַיִּחַר לְקַיִן מְאֹד וַיִּפְּלוּ פָּנָיו (בראשית ד:ה) [divergence] Inversion of the envy: the shepherd eyes the farmer's goods. ETCSL "enviously" is interpretive.
125 engar-ĝu₁₀ na-gada-zu {ĝiš}tukul-ta mu-un-sar-re איכרי את נוקדך בנשק מבריח וַיָּקָם קַיִן אֶל הֶבֶל אָחִיו וַיַּהַרְגֵהוּ (בראשית ד:ח) [divergence] The farmer attacks the herdsman with a weapon – drives him off the field; in Genesis kills him "in the field".
69–70 a-gar₃-a-gar₃-ra du₁₄ … mu₂; a-da-min₃ … ak בשדמה ובשדמה – ריב מצמיחות; ויכוח עושות וַיְהִי בִּהְיוֹתָם בַּשָּׂדֶה (בראשית ד:ח) [divergence] The quarrel of the two "sisters" breaks out over the fields, after wine and beer; it ends in a verdict and reconciliation (181–182), not murder.
192 a-da-min₃ dug₄-ga ויכוח שנאמר וַיֹּאמֶר קַיִן אֶל הֶבֶל אָחִיו (בראשית ד:ח) [absent] The Sumerian is all speech between the two; in Genesis Cain's words to Abel are not given.
181–182 nin₉ ḫe₂-me-eš; teš₂-bi-da ḫe₂-en-da-sug₂-sug₂-ge-eš אחיות תהיינה! יחדיו תעמודנה! הֲשֹׁמֵר אָחִי אָנֹכִי (בראשית ד:ט) [divergence] The god decrees sisterhood between shepherd's and farmer's product; Genesis' brothers end in murder and denial.
90 ĝa₂ udu e₂-ubur-ra an-edin-na la₂-a בית הצאן, דיר־החליבה, הנטויים בערבה העליונה הוּא הָיָה אֲבִי יֹשֵׁב אֹהֶל וּמִקְנֶה (בראשית ד:כ) [equivalent] The herders' pens "pitched" on the steppe.
4–5, 17–18, 46, 117–119 gu {d}uttu … dim₂; men; {d}niĝir-si; apin; bappir, titab חוט אוטו; כתר; ניגירסי; מחרשה; לחם־השכר לֹטֵשׁ כָּל חֹרֵשׁ נְחֹשֶׁת וּבַרְזֶל (בראשית ד:כב); אֲבִי כָּל תֹּפֵשׂ כִּנּוֹר וְעוּגָב (בראשית ד:כא) [divergence] Culture inventions: Genesis assigns them to human ancestors (Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-cain); here weaving, kingship, marriage (?), agriculture and brewing are gods and divine gifts.
20 nam-lu₂-ulu₃ ud re-a-ke₄-ne האנושות של הימים ההם הַנְּפִלִים הָיוּ בָאָרֶץ בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם (בראשית ו:ד) [equivalent] The same "those days" of primeval time; ud re has "days". Also ETCSL 1.7.6, 2.
36, 164 zi šag₄ … ĝal₂; niĝ₂-gu₇ מחיה נתנו; מאכל כְּיֶרֶק עֵשֶׂב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם אֶת כֹּל (בראשית ט:ג) [divergence] Flock and grain are given together at the beginning; in Genesis animal food is added only after the flood.
65–68 ĝeštin niĝ₂ dug₃ … naĝ יין, הדבר המתוק – שותות וַיֵּשְׁתְּ מִן הַיַּיִן וַיִּשְׁכָּר (בראשית ט:כא) [divergence] Wine (and beer) lead to the quarrel; Noah's wine to shame and a curse.
179 lu₂ lu₂-u₃ in-na-ab-e איש אל רעהו אומר וַיֹּאמְרוּ אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ (בראשית יא:ג) [equivalent] The same idiom.
182 teš₂-bi-da … sug₂ יחדיו תעמודנה וְלֹא נָשָׂא אֹתָם הָאָרֶץ לָשֶׁבֶת יַחְדָּו (בראשית יג:ו) [divergence] Abram and Lot separate; Sheep and Grain are ordered to stay together.
69 du₁₄ ריב וַיְהִי רִיב בֵּין רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה אַבְרָם וּבֵין רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה לוֹט (בראשית יג:ז) [equivalent] Quarrel over land between owners of flocks.
72, 184 dub-saĝ; gu-ul הראשונה; גדולה וְרַב יַעֲבֹד צָעִיר (בראשית כה:כג) [equivalent] A divine decision between two siblings which one is "great".
107 zulumḫi האדרת? כֻּלּוֹ כְּאַדֶּרֶת שֵׂעָר (בראשית כה:כה) [equivalent] The long-fleeced garment.
101 {ĝiš}pan; a-ma-ru (quiver) הקשתות; האשפה שָׂא נָא כֵלֶיךָ תֶּלְיְךָ וְקַשְׁתֶּךָ (בראשית כז:ג) [equivalent] Bow and quiver (of leather, from the sheep).
52 ḫe₂-ĝal₂ an-na-ta שפע מן השמים וְיִתֶּן לְךָ הָאֱלֹהִים מִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם וּמִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְרֹב דָּגָן וְתִירֹשׁ (בראשית כז:כח) [equivalent] Heaven's abundance and grain together.
175, 185 gu₂ … ĝa₂; dub₃ [ki]-a … za את צווארי ארצה … אָשִׂים; ברך [ארצה] תכרע הֱוֵה גְבִיר לְאַחֶיךָ וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְךָ בְּנֵי אִמֶּךָ (בראשית כז:כט) [equivalent] The sibling who must bow.
132–133 u₈ me-a … lu₂ mu-un-na-ab-be₂ איפה הכבשות? … אומר לאיש טְרֵפָה לֹא הֵבֵאתִי אֵלֶיךָ אָנֹכִי אֲחַטֶּנָּה (בראשית לא:לט) [equivalent] The herdsman accountable for every head.
123–131 the herder's dangers נחש, שודד, ספירה הָיִיתִי בַיּוֹם אֲכָלַנִי חֹרֶב וְקֶרַח בַּלָּיְלָה (בראשית לא:מ) [equivalent] The hardships of the herdsman's life (Jacob's speech).
136 e₂-ubur-ra … du₃ דיר־חליבה בונים וּלְמִקְנֵהוּ עָשָׂה סֻכֹּת (בראשית לג:יז) [equivalent] Shelter built for the flock.
51 saĝ zig₃ il₂-la-ni בשאתה ראש זקוף וַיִּשָּׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ שַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים (בראשית מ:כ) [equivalent] "Lifting the head". Weak.
145, 190–191 anše-kur-ra; lu₂ gud tuku lu₂ udu tuku … kan₄ lu₂ še tuku-e סוסים; איש אשר לו שור … בשער האיש אשר לו שעורה וַיִּתֵּן לָהֶם יוֹסֵף לֶחֶם בַּסּוּסִים וּבְמִקְנֵה הַצֹּאן וּבְמִקְנֵה הַבָּקָר (בראשית מז:יז); וְכָל הָאָרֶץ בָּאוּ מִצְרַיְמָה לִשְׁבֹּר (בראשית מא:נז) [equivalent] The owners of herds come to the owner of grain: the verdict's social picture is Joseph's Egypt. Our proposal.
105–106 i₃ dug₃-ga ir-sim diĝir-ra; i₃ šim … sa₂-dug₄ שמן טוב, ריח האלים; שמן בשמים … למנחות הקבועות וְעָשִׂיתָ אֹתוֹ שֶׁמֶן מִשְׁחַת קֹדֶשׁ (שמות ל:כה); וְעִשָּׂרֹן סֹלֶת בָּלוּל בְּשֶׁמֶן כָּתִית (שמות כט:מ) [equivalent] Oil for the gods and for the regular offerings.
110–111 gudug pa₄-šeš lu₂ a tu₅-am₃; šu-luḫ … mur₁₀ הכוהן … האיש הרחוץ במים; אחרי שאותי לבשו בִּגְדֵי קֹדֶשׁ הֵם וְרָחַץ בַּמַּיִם אֶת בְּשָׂרוֹ וּלְבֵשָׁם (ויקרא טז:ד) [equivalent] Bathed priests dress for the rite.
28 eš₃ ninda gu₇ diĝir-re-e-ne מקדש אכילת הלחם של האלים לֶחֶם אֱלֹהָיו (ויקרא כא:כב); אֶת קָרְבָּנִי לַחְמִי (במדבר כח:ב) [divergence] The gods eat bread before men do; in the Bible "God's bread" is the offering.
159–160 {im}šu-rin-na התנור וְאָפוּ עֶשֶׂר נָשִׁים לַחְמְכֶם בְּתַנּוּר אֶחָד (ויקרא כו:כו) [cognate] Sum. šu-rin-na < Akk. tinūru ~ תַּנּוּר.
131 ĝiš-šudum מקל־הספירה כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט (ויקרא כז:לב) [equivalent] Counting the flock with a stick.
46 apin … erin₂ מחרשה … צמדו לֹא תַחֲרֹשׁ בְּשׁוֹר וּבַחֲמֹר יַחְדָּו (דברים כב:י) [equivalent] Plough and team.
107, 111 siki; flax (gu, 4, 96) צמר; חוט לֹא תִלְבַּשׁ שַׁעַטְנֵז צֶמֶר וּפִשְׁתִּים יַחְדָּו (דברים כב:יא); בְּבֶגֶד צֶמֶר אוֹ בְּבֶגֶד פִּשְׁתִּים (ויקרא יג:מז) [equivalent] Wool and flax as the two cloth materials, both claimed by Sheep (96, Uttu's threads).
125 engar; na-gada איכר; נוקד וּמֵישַׁע מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב הָיָה נֹקֵד (מלכים ב ג:ד); אֲשֶׁר הָיָה בַנֹּקְדִים מִתְּקוֹעַ (עמוס א:א) [cognate] Loanwords: Sum. na-gada = Akk. nāqidu = נֹקֵד; Sum. engar > Akk. ikkaru > אִכָּר.
176 {ĝiš}ba-an סאה סְאָה סֹלֶת בְּשֶׁקֶל וְסָאתַיִם שְׂעֹרִים בְּשֶׁקֶל (מלכים ב ז:א) [equivalent] Grain measured and sold by the seah.
151 {ĝiš}tukul … ra בנשקו … היכה כִּי בַמַּטֶּה יֵחָבֶט קֶצַח (ישעיהו כח:כז); וַתַּחְבֹּט אֵת אֲשֶׁר לִקֵּטָה (רות ב:יז) [equivalent] Threshing by beating.
135, 153 tum₉ … sag₂; u₁₈-lu, mir הרוחות … זורות; רוח הדרום, רוח הצפון תִּזְרֵם וְרוּחַ תִּשָּׂאֵם (ישעיהו מא:טז) [equivalent] Winds and winnowing.
185 dub₃ … za ברך … תכרע כִּי לִי תִּכְרַע כָּל בֶּרֶךְ (ישעיהו מה:כג) [equivalent] Bowing the knee to the victor.
189 erin₂ {d}ezina₂-ka gu₂ … ĝar בצמד דגן – צוואר יָשִׂימוּ וְהַגּוֹי אֲשֶׁר יָבִיא אֶת צַוָּארוֹ בְּעֹל מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל (ירמיהו כז:יא) [equivalent] Submission as putting the neck in the yoke.
1, 27 ḫur-saĝ an ki; du₆ kug הר השמים והארץ; התל הטהור בְּעֵדֶן גַּן אֱלֹהִים הָיִיתָ … בְּהַר קֹדֶשׁ אֱלֹהִים הָיִיתָ (יחזקאל כח:יג–יד) [equivalent] The holy mountain/mound of the gods, place of riches, from which one descends.
111 tug₂ siki צמר בִּגְדֵי פִשְׁתִּים יִלְבָּשׁוּ; וְלֹא יַעֲלֶה עֲלֵיהֶם צֶמֶר (יחזקאל מד:יז) [divergence] Wool is the Sumerian priests' garment of purity; wool is forbidden to the priests in Ezekiel's temple (linen, Lev 16:4).
21, 24, 42 ninda; u₂; ed₃ לחם; עשב; מורידים מַצְמִיחַ חָצִיר לַבְּהֵמָה וְעֵשֶׂב לַעֲבֹדַת הָאָדָם; לְהוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ (תהלים קד:יד); וְלֶחֶם לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ יִסְעָד (תהלים קד:טו) [equivalent] Grass for beasts, bread for man; in the psalm bread comes "out of the earth", here down from the gods.
187–188 {d}utu e₃-a-ra {d}utu šu₂-uš-e mu {d}ezina₂-kam ḫe₂-em-pad₃-pad₃-de₃ מצאת אותו עד בוא אותו – שם דגן הוא אשר יינקב מִמִּזְרַח שֶׁמֶשׁ עַד מְבוֹאוֹ מְהֻלָּל שֵׁם יְהוָה (תהלים קיג:ג); כִּי מִמִּזְרַח שֶׁמֶשׁ וְעַד מְבוֹאוֹ גָּדוֹל שְׁמִי בַּגּוֹיִם (מלאכי א:יא) [equivalent] The same formula: from sunrise to sunset + the name. ETCSL's "praised" for pad₃; we יינקב.
59 e₂ ukur₃-ra saḫar ki us₂-sa בבית הדל, הדבק לעפר הארץ מְקִימִי מֵעָפָר דָּל (תהלים קיג:ז) [equivalent] The poor in the dust, lifted by the gift.
181 nin₉ ḫe₂-me-eš אחיות תהיינה הִנֵּה מַה טּוֹב וּמַה נָּעִים שֶׁבֶת אַחִים גַּם יָחַד (תהלים קלג:א) [equivalent] Siblings together.
66 kaš … dug₃-dug₃ שכר … מטיבות (בו את ליבן) וַיֹּאכַל בֹּעַז וַיֵּשְׁתְּ וַיִּיטַב לִבּוֹ (רות ג:ז) [equivalent] Drink "makes good" the heart.
31, 34 gu₇ … nu-mu-un-de₃-si-si-eš אוכלים – ולא נמלאו וְגַם הַנֶּפֶשׁ לֹא תִמָּלֵא (קהלת ו:ז); אָכוֹל וְאֵין לְשָׂבְעָה (חגי א:ו); וַאֲכַלְתֶּם וְלֹא תִשְׂבָּעוּ (ויקרא כו:כו) [equivalent] Eating without being filled – here of the gods, which is why they give the food away.
24 udu-gin₇ … u₂ … gu₇ כצאן … עשב אוכלים וְעִשְׂבָּא כְתוֹרִין יֵאכֻל (דניאל ד:ל) [equivalent] The man who eats grass like cattle is outside humanity.

Proposals for the shared renderings

  1. Personified goods: ezina₂ = דָּגָן, u₈ = כִּבְשָׂה as names (no article, feminine), ezina₂-kusu = דָּגָן־כּוּסוּ; the animal u₈ with the article where Hebrew needs it.
  2. Herding and farming (corpus §3, they touch Gen 4:2): sipad = רוֹעֶה; na-gada = נוֹקֵד [cognate loan]; engar = אִכָּר [cognate loan]; nam-sipad = רוֹעוּת; amaš = דִּיר; e₂-ubur = דִּיר־חֲלִיבָה; apin = מַחֲרֵשָׁה; šudul = עֹל; erin₂ = צֶמֶד; ab-sin₂ = תֶּלֶם; ki-du₆ = גֹּרֶן; ban = סְאָה; šu-rin-na = תַּנּוּר [cognate loan], udun = כִּבְשָׁן; ĝiš-šudum = מַקֵּל־הַסְּפִירָה. Never עֹבֵד/עֲבוֹדָה for any of them.
  3. Gift words kept apart from Gen 4:3–4: kadra = תְּשׁוּרָה; niĝ₂-ba = מַתָּנָה (text 2); מִנְחָה only for sa₂-dug₄ (texts 4–5) or a real offering term.
  4. Naming and "before": mu … zu = יָדַע שֵׁם (kept apart from mu sa₄ = קָרָא שֵׁם); plain nu- = לֹא, never טֶרֶם (now in texts 2 and 5); ud … -a-ba = בַּיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר / כַּאֲשֶׁר to be fixed corpus-wide (open decision 1).
  5. Nakedness and clothing: sug₄ (of limbs) = חָשׂוּף; עֵירֹם/עָרוּם stay reserved for a Sumerian/Akkadian word that means "naked" (Akk. erû/ūru, Sum. bar-dul₅? – to be checked when one occurs).
  6. Food words: zi-šag₄(-ĝal₂) = מִחְיָה; si (be filled) = נִמְלָא, not שָׂבַע; u₂-šim = מִסְפּוֹא; dug₃ (verb, of drink and friendship) = הֵיטִיב (לֵב); niĝ₂ dug₃ (of food/drink) = הַדָּבָר הַמָּתוֹק; i₃ = שֶׁמֶן (note "fat" at Gen 4:4 rows).
  7. Places: ḫur-saĝ = הַר; du₆ (kug) = (הַ)תֵּל (הַטָּהוֹר); kur (highland) = הָרִים / (foreign land) אֶרֶץ (text 2); bar-rim₄ (arid land) = צִיָּה vs. (dry land, opp. water) יַבָּשָׁה (text 2); an-edin = הָעֲרָבָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה; ki-ulutim₂ = מְקוֹם הוּלֶּדֶת.
  8. Names (§1): נִיגִּירְסִי, אִישְׁכּוּר (= אֲדַד), הַסַּג־אוּר־סַג, הַכֹּהֵן־הַגּוּדוּג, הַכֹּהֵן־הַפָּשֵׁשׁ.
  9. Guidelines §6.7 (traps): plural שדמות contains דמות (use שְׁדֵמוֹת only vocalized, or a construction); בשמים "spices" vs "in heaven" – always vocalize בְּשָׂמִים; חלבו "his milk" vs "his fat" (Gen 4:4!) – vocalize; שכנו "dwelt" vs the name שַׁכַּן – vocalize; דגן contains גן (harmless).

Lessons for the guidelines

  • ETCSL's lemma can contradict ETCSL's translation in exactly the key line. In 27/39 ETCSL lemmatizes se₁₂ "to live (pl.)" but translates "created" – and the "creation of grain and sheep" in the secondary literature rests on that translation. In 25 the lemma is "garden", the translation "ditches"; in 1 the word is "mountain", the brief and the literature say "hill". Read the lemma line before the translation, and list such contradictions in the parallels index.
  • When ORACC has no text, build a form index of the whole ORACC corpus (form → cf, gw, morph, text, line) and look up every verbal form of the ETCSL text: here 99 of 198 distinct verbal forms have a parsed instance elsewhere (the "like sheep they eat grass" line itself in How Grain came to Sumer). Mark the rest as "our analysis". The throw-away scripts (session scratchpad): lem.py (ETCSL TEI → per-line form=lemma[label]), buildidx.py + q.py/morph.py (ORACC form index and per-line morph lookup), conc.py (ETCSL bulk concordance with the translation paragraph), gl.py (ePSD2 glossary regex lookup) – again a case for tools/sumerian_workbench.py.
  • Search the formula across genres before drafting a "unique" line: the primeval humans "eating grass with their mouths like sheep" (24) is the first line of How Grain came to Sumer (1.7.6); the debate colophon finds Dumuzid and Enkimdu (4.08.33), the shepherd–farmer dispute whose verdict (for the shepherd) is the Genesis one.
  • Loanwords are the Sumerian [cognate]s: Sumerian has no Semitic roots, but words that travelled through Akkadian into Hebrew (engar → אִכָּר, na-gada = נֹקֵד, šu-rin-na ~ תַּנּוּר) are real lexical links and should be rendered by their Hebrew descendants and tagged.
  • Personified commodities need a grammatical decision before drafting (gender, article): Hebrew דָּגָן is masculine, the Sumerian Grain is a sister and a maiden; decide it once (here: name, feminine, no article) and say so in both introductions.
  • Draft unvocalized from the first line – this session repeated text 3's mistake for 42 lines (a fully vocalized draft) and had to rewrite them; the rule should be the first line of the translator's brief, not one item among many.

Text 6: The Founding of Eridu (CT 13 35–38)

Scope

  • Text: the bilingual Sumerian–Akkadian incantation Ē elli bīt ilī / e₂ ku₃-ga e₂ diĝir-e-ne ("The pure house, the house of the gods"), known as "The Creation of the World by Marduk" or "The Founding of Eridu": a cosmogony (obverse) that serves as the mythical introduction to a ritual of purifying a temple – by the reverse, Ezida, Nabû's temple at Borsippa (eBL genre: Magic: Varia: Building Rituals). One tablet: BM 93014 + 82-3-23,101 (Late Babylonian; copy CT 13 35–38; the join by Borger 1988). A transliteration search of eBL (2026-10-16) found no duplicate.
  • Lines: all 67 entries – obv. 1–40 (the cosmogony, all translated) and rev. 1′–27′ (fragmentary; every legible word translated; rev. 1′–2′ and the broken Sumerian words of 3′, 6′, 11′ given as …). Labels as eBL: obv. 1 … obv. 40 (= King's), rev. 1' … rev. 27' (King rev. n ≈ eBL (n+9)′; eBL rev. 1′–9′ come from the joined fragment and are not in King).
  • Files: annotated-6-Founding-of-Eridu.rtl.md (Hebrew header incl. the bilingual convention and the {שומרית} tags; 8 sections; per line our Akkadian normalization ‖ eBL's transliteration, then the Sumerian halves; parsing of every Akkadian word and brief Sumerian parsing; King 1902; parallels; notes); translation-6-Founding-of-Eridu.rtl.md (introduction, the same sections, 13 footnotes), generated from the annotated file by a scratch builder (session scratchpad), so that the numbered lines equal the > lines; python3 -I verify.py 6 → OK.
  • Content: a chain of negations – no pure house, no reed, no tree, no brick or brick-mould, no house, no city, no nammaššû, no Nippur/Ekur, Uruk/Eanna, Apsû/Eridu (1–9); "all the lands were sea", the spring in the sea only a channel (10–11); then Eridu and Esagil, Babylon and Esagil, the Anunnakkū and the holy city (12–16); Marduk binds a reed raft on the face of the waters, "builds" dust and pours it beside the raft, to settle the gods (17–19); he builds mankind; Aruru builds the seed of mankind with him; the animals of Šakkan in the steppe; Tigris and Euphrates, set in place and named well; reeds, marsh plants, forest; the green of the steppe; "the lands were marsh and reed-bed"; cattle and sheep; gardens and forests; the he-goat and wild ram stand for him (20–30); Marduk fills a terrace at the sea's edge, [Ea?] sets reed-bed and dry land; something is "brought into being" (31–33); and the negations of 2–7 are reversed in the same order (34–40). Reverse: fragments of hymnic epithets (1′–12′), Papsukkal and Ningirima purify the addressee with censer, torch and Apsû water by Marduk's spell; abundance and rites for ever; Ezida, beloved of Anu and Ištar; "pure as heaven, clean as earth"; the evil tongue out; rubric; catch-line Ereqqu 2 (13′–27′).

Sources consulted

  • Rank 1: eBL Fragmentarium BM 93014 (../../sources/eBL-fragmentarium/atf/BM.93014.atf, raw json/BM.93014.json; not lemmatised, "not collated"). The Akkadian is normalized by us; every line gives our normalization and eBL's transliteration side by side.
  • Rank 2: the eBL dictionary API (= CDA), per word: amu "raft, usu. of reed", rāṭu "water-channel, pipe", īnu, uššu (III "dead reed"), appāru "reed-bed, marsh", apu "reed-bed; reeds", qīšu "forest", kirû, littu, būru II "calf", mīru "breeding bull", laḫru "ewe", puḫādu, immeru, supūru "sheepfold", atūdu "wild sheep; ram", sappāru "wild ram", tamlû ("filling"), pāṭu, nābalu "dry land, mainland" [PA.RI.IM], nammaštû "moving things, animals" [Á.DAM; NÍG.ZI.GÁL], šiknu, ramû, mitḫāriš, ṣīriš, ṭūbu (ṭ. libbi), agubbû, gizillû, ebbu, nuḫšu, ereqqu (e. šamê "Ursa Minor"), eršu, ušumgallu, kiššatu. Not found in eBL: dittu in a plant sense (rendered גֹּמֶא?). Corpus renderings, Enūma eliš renderings (rakāsu רָכַס, šapāku שָׁפַךְ, ramû הִתְיַשֵּׁב, mitḫāriš יַחְדָּיו, ṣīru נַעֲלֶה, eršu פִּקֵּחַ, māliku מְיַעֵץ, nuḫšu עֲתֶרֶת, ana ṣâti לָעַד, šiptu קֶסֶם, tû לַחַשׁ, Gilima גִּילִימָה, Lugaldukuga), texts 1–5 (Adapa šuklulu שִׁכְלֵל, zēr amīlūti זֶרַע הָאֱנוֹשׁוּת, sukkallu וְזִיר; Sumerian dim₂ עִצֵּב, du₃ בָּנָה, ĝar שָׂם, kug/sikil טָהוֹר/זַךְ, u₃-šub מַלְבֵּן, a-gar₃, bar-rim₄).
  • No rank 3 is available: Lambert 2013 (Babylonian Creation Myths, 361–365), Ambos 2004 (Mesopotamische Baurituale, 199–212) and Heidel 1951 (The Babylonian Genesis, 61–63) are not owned; no pirate copies were searched for. The Hebrew rests on our own reading of eBL's transliteration.
  • Rank 5: King 1902, vol. I 130–139 (../../sources/King-1902--Seven-Tablets-of-Creation/vol-1_djvu.txt, from l. 14600), read after each line; quoted in every entry. King's main outdated readings: 1 "in the holy place" (eBL has no elli in the Akkadian), 11 "a movement in the sea" (rāṭu "channel"), 17 "a reed" (amu "raft"), 19 šubat (not in eBL's Akkadian), 32 na-ma-la "marsh" (eBL na-ba-la = nābalu "dry land"), rev. 14′ "Nin-aha-kudu" (eBL Ningirim).
  • Comparison: the commentary on Gen 1:2, 1:9–10 (1010-…: וְתֵרָאֶה as a "medial" Nifal, "a development that happened by itself"), 1:26–28, 2:4–17 (1020-…), 2:18–3:24, 4:1–17 (skimmed); Enūma eliš VI 1–66 (../1-אנומה-אליש/translation-VI.rtl.md); text 5 (the "not" chain, שָׁכְנוּ? / SIG₇).

Decisions

  1. Bilingual convention (project Decision 5, as specified by the coordinator's brief): the Akkadian is translated wherever it survives; the Sumerian is parsed in the apparatus and its differences noted there. A line whose Hebrew comes from the Sumerian begins with {שומרית} (a recension-style tag, guidelines §6.8). Extension: where only part of a line survives in Sumerian (obv. 37, 39, 40: the Akkadian half is restored or lost), the tag encloses only the words translated from the Sumerian, {שומרית: …}; also for the rubric en₂ "incantation" at obv. 1, which is Sumerian only. Explained in both headers. (Decision 5 had excluded {שומרית: …} for differences; here it marks provenance, so the two uses do not collide.)
  2. Reverse with separate-line pairs (12′/13′, 17′/18′, 22′/23′): each tablet line is one entry translated from its own language, so the Sumerian line gets {שומרית} and the next line the Akkadian; the content is therefore given twice, as on the tablet.
  3. No טֶרֶם. Obv. 1–9 have ul + stative (ul epuš, ul aṣi, ul bani, ul nadât, ul banât, ul šakin, ul epšet): "was not made/built", not "not yet" (Akkadian would use adīni); King's "had not yet" is interpretive. Rendered with the Hebrew Nifal/Hophal and vocalized (נַעֲשָׂה, נִבְנָה, הוּטְלָה, הוּשַׂם) – unvocalized נעשה also reads נַעֲשֶׂה "let us make" (Gen 1:26). The Gen 2:5 row is [divergence]; Prov 8:26 עַד-לֹא עָשָׂה is the closer [equivalent]. Same policy as texts 2 and 5.
  4. Creation verbs: banû = בָּנָה everywhere (17 preserved occurrences + 3 restored – reed, tree, brick-mould, city, temples, dust, mankind, the seed of mankind, animals, rivers, plants); ibtani parsed as G perfect (formally also Gt preterite; no reciprocal sense; LB narrative perfect); epēšu = עָשָׂה (10 + 3: house, city, cities, Apsû, gods); šubšû = הֵבִיא לִכְלַל הֲוָיָה once (33). The bilingual maps the Sumerian verbs systematically: Sum. dim₂ → Akk. banû, Sum. du₃ → Akk. epēšu, and twice Sum. mu₂ "grow" → banû (18, 21); in the {שומרית} segments the Sumerian verbs keep their project renderings (dim₂ עִצֵּב, du₃ בָּנָה).
  5. Echo decisions: ina pān mê = עַל פְּנֵי הַמַּיִם [cognate] (the preposition by meaning: on the surface); nābalu (Sum. pa-rim₄) = יַבָּשָׁה [equivalent], because the word means "dry land" as opposed to the sea (eBL; the Sumerian agrees), unlike text 5's bar-rim₄ "arid land" (צִיָּה); šikin napišti (Sum. niĝ₂-zi-ĝal₂ "that which has life") = בַּעֲלֵי נֶפֶשׁ (נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה reserved; נֶפֶשׁ kept as the cognate of napištu); eperu = עָפָר; urqītu = יֶרֶק; kirû = גַּן (tagged); ṭūb libbi = טוּב לֵב [cognate]; ṭābiš = הֵיטֵב (root of טוֹב).
  6. New cognate renderings: rāṭu = רַהַט (Gen 30:38; vocalized: modern "furniture"); īnu = עַיִן (eye/spring); tamlû + malû D = מִלּוֹא מִלֵּא (the Millo); laḫru = רָחֵל; atūdu = עַתּוּד; rakāsu = רָכַס (EE); šapāku = שָׁפַךְ (EE). Others: amu = רַפְסוֹדָה (2 Chr 2:15); appāru = אֲגַם; apu = סוּף (so that קָנֶה stays for qanû); dittu = גֹּמֶא?; uššu = קָנֶה־יָבֵשׁ?; qīšu/qīštu = יַעַר; littu פָּרָה, būru עֵגֶל, mīru פַּר, puḫādu טָלֶה, immeru כֶּבֶשׂ, supūru דִּיר, sappāru אֵיל־הַבָּר; pāṭ tâmti = שְׂפַת הַיָּם; ṣīriš = בְּרוֹמְמוּת; mitḫāriš = יַחְדָּיו; ramû = הִתְיַשֵּׁב.
  7. Ritual vocabulary (reverse): ellu = טָהוֹר, ebbu = זַךְ (as Sum. kug/sikil, text 2); elēlu D = טִהֵר; ubbubu = זִכֵּךְ; niqnakku = מִקְטֶרֶת; gizillû = לַפִּיד; agubbû = אַגַּן־הַמַּיִם; tû = לַחַשׁ, šiptu/en₂ = קֶסֶם (EE); ka-inim-ma = נֻסַּח־הַקֶּסֶם; nuḫšu = עֲתֶרֶת (EE; שֶׁפַע = ḫegallu); ana ūmī ṣâti = לִימֵי עַד (EE ana ṣâti לָעַד; never לְעוֹלָם); kalālu Št = יִשְׁתַּכְלְלוּ; kiššatu = כָּל; sukkallu = וְזִיר; eršu (Sum. galanzu) = פִּקֵּחַ; māliku = מְיַעֵץ; ereqqi šamê = עֲגָלַת הַשָּׁמַיִם (Ursa Minor).
  8. Cruxes kept visible: obv. 15 (singular īpuš "he made the gods" vs. the Sumerian ergative plural "the gods built"): Hebrew keeps the Akkadian singular and the ambiguity, with ?; obv. 32 eBL's restoration [{d}IDIM tâm]ta shown as [אֵאָה? את הים?]; obv. 18′ ullu = טִהֲרָה?; obv. 25 plant names with ?.
  9. Names: מַרְדּוּךְ (Sum. Gilima גִּילִימָה at 17, Asalluḫi at 31, 19′ – in the apparatus); אֲרוּרוּ (note: not אָרוּר); שַׁכַּן; הָאֲנוּנָּכִּי; לוּגַל־דּוּכּוּגָּה (the full Sumerian form; EE VII has לוּגַל־דּוּכּוּ); אֵסַגִּיל, אֵכּוּר, אֵאַנָּה, נִיפּוּר, אוּרוּךְ (= אֶרֶךְ), אֶרִידוּ, הָאַפְּסוּ, בָּבֶל; פַּפְּסוּכַּל; נִינְגִּירִימָה; אֵזִידָה; אָנוּ, אִשְׁתַּר (Sum. אַן, אִינַנָּה).
  10. Letter-sequence check of the > lines: no ברא, בראש, שבת, דמות, נשמ, עבד, אדמ, טרם, עדן, תהום, לעולם; נעשה occurs only as vocalized נַעֲשָׂה (Decision 3); קרא only for nabû (16, 24). שָׂם (šakānu, ĝar) always vocalized; בַּמָּקוֹם vocalized (unvocalized also "instead of"); שְׁמָן vocalized ("oil").

Open decisions for the user

  1. Buy or borrow Lambert 2013 (361–365) and Ambos 2004 (199–212): the only modern editions; they would settle obv. 11 (rāṭu), 15, 25 (uššu, dittu), 30 (izzazzūšu), 32 (the restoration and nābalu), 33, and the reverse 1′–12′.
  2. obv. 32 nābalu = יַבָּשָׁה (followed: the meaning, and the Sumerian pa-rim₄ agrees) or a word that does not pre-empt Gen 1:9–10 (חָרָבָה, אֲדָמָה יְבֵשָׁה). A corpus rule for "dry land" is needed (text 2 הַיַּבָּשָׁה, text 5 צִיָּה).
  3. obv. 15: "he (Marduk) made the gods together" (Akkadian singular, King) or "the gods built (it) together" (Sumerian ergative; cf. Enūma eliš VI 57–62).
  4. obv. 22 בַּעֲלֵי נֶפֶשׁ (followed) or יְצוּרֵי חַיִּים / חַיִּים – the latter avoid the Gen 1:24/1:30 נֶפֶשׁ but lose the cognate.
  5. obv. 11 רַהַט (cognate, Gen 30:38; followed) or the neutral צִנּוֹר.
  6. The {שומרית: …} segment tag (Decision 1) – confirm, or prefer a footnote for partly Sumerian lines.
  7. קֶסֶם for en₂/šiptu follows project 1's open decision 4 (alternative לַחַשׁ for both, or חֶבֶר). Settled 2026-10-21 (cross-corpus harmonization): šiptu = קֶסֶם, Akk. tû = לַחַשׁ (rev. 19′ keeps בלחש: its Akkadian is tû).
  8. Print stub and the combined translation.rtl.md are the coordinator's (not created here).

Progress log

obv. 10 napḫar mātāti tâmtum-ma כל הארצות – ים (היו) וְחֹשֶׁךְ עַל פְּנֵי תְהוֹם (בראשית א:ב) [equivalent] Before the land, everything is water. tâmtu (cognate of תְּהוֹם) is rendered יָם; the link is in the apparatus only.
obv. 8 apsû ul epuš האפסו לא נעשה וְחֹשֶׁךְ עַל פְּנֵי תְהוֹם (בראשית א:ב) [divergence] Even the subterranean water (Apsû) "was not made": there is no pre-existing deep, only sea.
obv. 17 Marduk ama ina pān mê irkus מרדוך רפסודה על פני המים רכס וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם (בראשית א:ב) [cognate] The same phrase (pānu = פנים, mû = מים), at the same stage. There the spirit hovers; here the god binds a reed raft – manual work. The Sumerian names him Gilima, "the binder" (EE VII 80).
obv. 10, 27 tâmtum-ma; mātāti appāri apum-ma ים (היו); הארצות – אגם וסוף (היו) יִקָּווּ הַמַּיִם מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמַיִם אֶל מָקוֹם אֶחָד וְתֵרָאֶה הַיַּבָּשָׁה (בראשית א:ט) [divergence] The lands pass from sea (10) to marsh and reed-bed (27): gradual emergence, no gathering of the waters, no command. Our proposal (the 10 ↔ 27 pairing).
obv. 18, 31, 32 eperī ibni … išpuk; tamlâ umalli; apa nābala iškun עפר בנה ושפך; מלוא מלא; סוף ויבשה שׂם וְתֵרָאֶה הַיַּבָּשָׁה (בראשית א:ט) [divergence] The dry land is made by labour – dust built and poured beside the raft, a fill at the sea's edge, dry land "set" – where Gen 1:9 has the medial Nifal "let it appear" (the commentary's "development that happened by itself", 1010-…). Our proposal. 32 rests partly on eBL's restoration.
obv. 32 nābalu (Sum. pa-rim₄) יבשה וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לַיַּבָּשָׁה אֶרֶץ (בראשית א:י) [equivalent] The word itself: dry land as against sea. eBL reads na-ba-la (King na-ma-la "marsh"); the Sumerian pa-rim₄ confirms. Open decision 2.
obv. 24 šumšina ṭābiš imbi (Sum. nam-dug₃ … sa₄) את שמן היטב קרא וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לַיַּבָּשָׁה אֶרֶץ וּלְמִקְוֵה הַמַּיִם קָרָא יַמִּים; וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי טוֹב (בראשית א:י) [cognate] Naming and "good" together, of waters (the rivers). ṭābiš ~ טוֹב; nabû ↔ קָרָא [equivalent]. Our proposal.
obv. 25, 34 uššu ditta appāri qanâ u qīšu ibtani; qanâ iṣa ibtani קנה־יבש?, גומא? האגם, קנה ויער בנה; קנה, עץ – בנה תַּדְשֵׁא הָאָרֶץ דֶּשֶׁא (בראשית א:יא) [divergence] Plants are "built" by the god (marsh plants and forest); in Gen 1:11 the earth brings them forth.
obv. 22 šikin napišti (Sum. niĝ₂-zi-ĝal₂) בעלי נפש תּוֹצֵא הָאָרֶץ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה לְמִינָהּ (בראשית א:כד) [cognate] napištu = נֶפֶשׁ; the Sumerian "that which has life" ≈ אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה (א:ל). נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה itself is reserved.
obv. 28 littu būrša mīru laḫru puḫādsa immer supūri פרה ועגלה, פר; רחל וטליה, כבש הדיר וַיַּעַשׂ אֱלֹהִים אֶת חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ לְמִינָהּ וְאֶת הַבְּהֵמָה לְמִינָהּ (בראשית א:כה) [equivalent] Wild animals (22) then domestic cattle and sheep (28): the order of Gen 1:25. laḫru = רָחֵל [cognate].
obv. 20 amēlūta ibtani את האנושות בנה וַיִּבְרָא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם בְּצַלְמוֹ (בראשית א:כז) [equivalent] One line, no material, no purpose, no image; contrast Enūma eliš VI and KAR 4 (blood, toil).
obv. 21 Aruru … ittišu ibtanû ארורו … עמו בנתה זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה בָּרָא אֹתָם (בראשית א:כז) [divergence] The creators are male and female (Marduk with Aruru); in Gen 1:27 the created.
obv. 30 atūdu šappāru izzazzūšu העתוד, איל־הבר – עומדים לו וּרְדוּ בִּדְגַת הַיָּם וּבְעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וּבְכָל חַיָּה הָרֹמֶשֶׂת עַל הָאָרֶץ (בראשית א:כח) [divergence] The wild animals stand in the god's service, not under man's rule. Our proposal (izuzzu + dative). The Sumerian says "he made (them) abundant".
obv. 33 […] uštabši (Sum. mu-un-tuku) […] הביא לכלל הוויה וַיִּבְרָא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הַתַּנִּינִם הַגְּדֹלִים (בראשית א:כא) [equivalent] šubšû, the closest Akkadian verb to בָּרָא, once in the text; its object is lost.
obv. 15–19 ilū Anunnakkū … īpuš; ilī … ana šušubi האלים, האנונכי – יחדיו עשה?; את האלים … להושיב וַיְכֻלּוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ וְכָל צְבָאָם (בראשית ב:א) [absent] The gods are made (or build) after Babylon, and the land is made to settle them in "heart's delight"; Genesis has no other gods.
obv. 1–9 ul epuš, ul aṣi, ul bani, ul nadât, ul šakin, ul epšet לא נעשה, לא יצא, לא נבנה, לא הוטלה, לא הושׂם וְכֹל שִׂיחַ הַשָּׂדֶה טֶרֶם יִהְיֶה בָאָרֶץ וְכָל עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה טֶרֶם יִצְמָח (בראשית ב:ה) [divergence] No "not yet": ul + stative = "was not made". The chain is of culture (house, city, temple, brick, reed) – not of plants, rain and worker.
obv. 26 urqīt ṣēri ibtani ירק הערבה בנה וְכָל עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה טֶרֶם יִצְמָח (בראשית ב:ה) [equivalent] "Green of the steppe" ↔ "herb of the field" (ṣēru ↔ שָׂדֶה); made by the god after man, without rain or labour. urqītu = יֶרֶק [cognate] (אֶת כָּל יֶרֶק עֵשֶׂב, א:ל).
— — — כִּי לֹא הִמְטִיר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים עַל הָאָרֶץ וְאָדָם אַיִן לַעֲבֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה (בראשית ב:ה) [absent] No rain and no task for man: mankind is built (20) without any purpose stated – unlike KAR 4, Atra-ḫasīs and Enūma eliš.
obv. 11 īnu ša qereb tâmti rāṭum-ma העין אשר בקרב הים – רהט (הייתה) וְאֵד יַעֲלֶה מִן הָאָרֶץ וְהִשְׁקָה אֶת כָּל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה (בראשית ב:ו) [divergence] The source of fresh water is only a "channel" within the sea; in Gen 2:6 it rises from the earth and waters the ground.

obv. 13, 19 Lugaldukuga irmû; ilī … ana šušubi לוגל־דוכוגה התיישב; את האלים … להושיב וַיָּשֶׂם שָׁם אֶת הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר יָצָר (בראשית ב:ח) [divergence] The first place made is a god's dwelling, and the land is made to settle the gods; in Gen 2:8, 15 God places man.

obv. 22 būl Šakkan … ina ṣēri חית שכן … בערבה וַיִּצֶר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים מִן הָאֲדָמָה כָּל חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה (בראשית ב:יט) [equivalent] "Animals of the steppe" ↔ "beasts of the field", after man.
— — — וַיִּקְרָא הָאָדָם שֵׁמוֹת לְכָל הַבְּהֵמָה (בראשית ב:כ) [absent] The god names (rivers, city); man names nothing.
obv. 20 ibtani בנה וַיִּבֶן יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶת הַצֵּלָע (בראשית ב:כב) [cognate] banû = בנה: the Akkadian verb of man's creation is the Genesis verb of woman's.
obv. 21 zēr amēlūti זרע האנושות וּבֵין זַרְעֲךָ וּבֵין זַרְעָהּ (בראשית ג:טו) [cognate] "The seed of mankind" built by the mother goddess.
obv. 21 Aruru ארורו כִּי הִוא הָיְתָה אֵם כָּל חָי (בראשית ג:כ) [equivalent] The birth goddess shares in creating mankind. Aruru ≠ אָרוּר.

Our proposal.
obv. 28 immer supūri כבש הדיר וַיְהִי הֶבֶל רֹעֵה צֹאן (בראשית ד:ב) [divergence] Flocks and fold belong to creation itself, not to a human occupation.
obv. 4, 12, 14, 37 ālu ul bani; Eridu epuš; Bābili epuš עיר לא נבנתה; ארידו נעשתה; בבל נעשתה וַיְהִי בֹּנֶה עִיר (בראשית ד:יז) [divergence] The city precedes man (12–16 before 20); in Genesis the first city is Cain's.

obv. 7 Uruk אורוך וַתְּהִי רֵאשִׁית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ בָּבֶל וְאֶרֶךְ וְאַכַּד (בראשית י:י) [cognate] Babylon and Uruk among the primeval cities.
obv. 3, 36 libittu; nalbantu לבנה; מלבן הָבָה נִלְבְּנָה לְבֵנִים (בראשית יא:ג) [cognate] Brick and mould belong to creation; in Gen 11 a human invention.

obv. 31 ina pāṭ tâmti בשפת הים וְכַחוֹל אֲשֶׁר עַל שְׂפַת הַיָּם (בראשית כב:יז) [equivalent] Idiom.
obv. 11 īnu העין הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי נִצָּב עַל עֵין הַמָּיִם (בראשית כד:יג) [cognate] "Eye" = spring in both languages.
obv. 11 rāṭu רהט בָּרְהָטִים בְּשִׁקְתוֹת הַמָּיִם (בראשית ל:לח) [cognate] Water channels (BDB compares Akk. rāṭu).
obv. 30 atūdu העתוד וְהִנֵּה הָעַתֻּדִים הָעֹלִים עַל הַצֹּאן (בראשית לא:י) [cognate]
obv. 28 laḫru רחל רְחֵלֶיךָ וְעִזֶּיךָ לֹא שִׁכֵּלוּ (בראשית לא:לח) [cognate]
obv. 27 apu סוף וַתָּשֶׂם בַּסּוּף עַל שְׂפַת הַיְאֹר (שמות ב:ג) [equivalent] Reed-bed at the water's edge.
obv. 17 rakāsu רכס וְיִרְכְּסוּ אֶת הַחֹשֶׁן (שמות כח:כח) [cognate]
obv. 18 eperī … išpuk עפר … שפך וְשָׁפְכוּ אֶת הֶעָפָר אֲשֶׁר הִקְצוּ (ויקרא יד:מא) [cognate] šapāku = שפך, of dust.
rev. 18′ ina agubbê elli ša apsî באגן־המים הטהור של האפסו וְרָחַץ בַּמַּיִם אֶת בְּשָׂרוֹ (ויקרא טז:ד) [equivalent] Purification with water before entering the holy.
obv. 1 ul epuš לא נעשה עַד-לֹא עָשָׂה אֶרֶץ וְחוּצוֹת (משלי ח:כו) [equivalent] The closest biblical "before" chain: negated עשה (= epēšu), in a sequence of "before the deeps … before the mountains" (Prov 8:24–26).
obv. 31 tamlâ umalli מלוא מלא וַיִּבֶן דָּוִד סָבִיב מִן הַמִּלּוֹא (שמואל ב ה:ט) [cognate] The Millo = an earth fill; the same root and figure.
obv. 17 amu רפסודה וּנְבִיאֵם לְךָ רַפְסֹדוֹת עַל יָם יָפוֹ (דברי הימים ב ב:טו) [equivalent] Raft on the sea.
rev. 15′ niqnakku מקטרת וּבְיָדוֹ מִקְטֶרֶת לְהַקְטִיר (דברי הימים ב כו:יט) [equivalent] Censer in the temple.
obv. 25, 27 appāru אגם וְהָיָה הַשָּׁרָב לַאֲגַם … חָצִיר לְקָנֶה וָגֹמֶא (ישעיהו לה:ז) [equivalent] Marsh, reed and rush together.
obv. 32 apa nābala iškun סוף ויבשה שׂם אָשִׂים מִדְבָּר לַאֲגַם מַיִם (ישעיהו מא:יח) [equivalent] "Set X (as) Y" with שׂים, in the opposite direction (desert → marsh).
obv. 16, 19 ṭūb libbi טוב לב הִנֵּה עֲבָדַי יָרֹנּוּ מִטּוּב לֵב (ישעיהו סה:יד) [cognate] The idiom.
rev. 23′ Ezida šubtu ṣīrtu narām libbi אזידה, מושב נעלה, אהוב לב וְשַׁבְתִּי בְּבֵית-יְהוָה לְאֹרֶךְ יָמִים (תהלים כג:ו) [equivalent] The temple as dwelling. Weak.
rev. 27′ ereqqi šamāmī עגלת השמים עֹשֶׂה-עָשׁ כְּסִיל וְכִימָה (איוב ט:ט) [equivalent] The Wagon (Ursa); עָשׁ/עַיִשׁ traditionally the Bear. Weak.

Proposals for the shared renderings

  1. Stative negation: ul + stative = לֹא + Nifal/Hophal, vocalized (לֹא נַעֲשָׂה), never טֶרֶם (now texts 2, 5, 6); add to corpus §3 the trap נעשה = נַעֲשָׂה / נַעֲשֶׂה.
  2. "Dry land": a corpus rule – nābalu / Sum. pa-rim₄, bar-rim₄ "dry land as against water" = יַבָּשָׁה [equivalent, tagged]; bar-rim₄ "arid land" = צִיָּה (text 5).
  3. Cognates for guidelines §6.7: rāṭu = רַהַט; tamlû = מִלּוֹא; laḫru = רָחֵל; atūdu = עַתּוּד; ṭūb libbi = טוּב לֵב; īnu = עַיִן (spring); karû = כְּרִי (text 7).
  4. šikin napišti / Sum. niĝ₂-zi-ĝal₂ = בַּעֲלֵי נֶפֶשׁ (keeps נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה reserved).
  5. Ritual pair ellu / ebbu = טָהוֹר / זַךְ (parallel to Sum. kug / sikil); elēlu D = טִהֵר, ubbubu = זִכֵּךְ; agubbû = אַגַּן־הַמַּיִם; gizillû = לַפִּיד; niqnakku = מִקְטֶרֶת.
  6. Time: ana ūmī ṣâti = לִימֵי עַד; ana ūmī dārûti = לִימֵי נֶצַח (text 7) – both never לְעוֹלָם.
  7. Names (§1): לוּגַל־דּוּכּוּגָּה (full form; EE לוּגַל־דּוּכּוּ), גִּילִימָה, פַּפְּסוּכַּל, נִינְגִּירִימָה, אֵזִידָה.
  8. The {שומרית} / {שומרית: …} tags for bilinguals → guidelines §6.8.

Lessons for the guidelines

  • A bilingual shows the ancient translators' own verb equations: Sum. dim₂ → Akk. banû, du₃ → epēšu, mu₂ "grow" → banû, tuku "acquire" → šubšû. In a bilingual, count the creation verbs per language before building a parallel on one of them.
  • An unlemmatised eBL ATF can be a base text: normalize it ourselves and print our normalization beside eBL's transliteration (normalization ‖ ATF), so that the reader can check every choice; parse every word with the eBL API; and say plainly in both headers that no rank-3 translation was available.
  • Statives in creation texts must be vocalized: נעשה, נבנה read both as "was made/built" and "let us make/build" – exactly the Gen 1:26 contrast.
  • Old editions misread exactly the key words (King: rāṭu "movement", amu "reed", nābalu "marsh"); list them line by line, since the comparative literature (Heidel, Gunkel) argued from them.
  • check_bible_quotes.py: a backticked non-biblical word followed by a reference in parentheses is checked as a quotation (and fails); keep our renderings and references apart.

Text 7: KAR 4

Scope

  • Text: KAR 4, the bilingual Sumerian–Akkadian account of the creation of man ("When heaven had been separated from earth"; older title "the creation of man from the blood of the Lamga gods"). Three manuscripts (SEAL): A VAT 9307 (Assur, Middle Assyrian; scribe Kidin-Sîn, apprentice, son of the king's scribe Sutê), the only complete one; B K 4175 + Sm 57 + 80-7-19,184 (+) 82-3-23,146 (Nineveh, Ashurbanipal's library); C A 17643 (Chicago; eBL writes A 17634), a few lines (25–29). In A and B each line is preceded by a column of the Syllable Alphabet (a school exercise; not translated); B's colophon calls the tablet "tablet 2 of ME.ME PAP.PAP", i.e. part of a scholastic compilation headed by the syllabary.
  • Lines: all 84 entries – obv. 1–9, 9a (B only), 10–41; rev. 1–30; colophon A rev. 31–32; colophon B 1–10. Labels: SEAL's numbers with obv./rev. prefixes (SEAL restarts at rev. 1); colophon B numbered by us in SEAL's order (eBL: K 4175 col. 4, 5–10). One entry per composite line; manuscript differences in the apparatus.
  • Files: annotated-7-KAR-4.rtl.md (header; 9 sections; per line SEAL's Akkadian transliteration by manuscript, then the Sumerian, eBL's readings where they differ; parsing with our normalization; SEAL's translation; parallels; notes); translation-7-KAR-4.rtl.md (introduction, 19 footnotes), generated from the annotated file; python3 -I verify.py 7 → OK.
  • Content: after heaven was separated from earth, the gods and goddesses "dwelt" (?), the earth was "built", the designs of heaven and earth made firm, dykes and canals ordered, the banks of Tigris and Euphrates set (1–6); An, Enlil, Utu (Šamaš), Enki (Ea), the Anunna(kkū) sit on the lofty dais and deliberate (7–11); "the designs of heaven and earth … dyke and canal … Tigris and Euphrates – they are established: what shall we do? what shall we build?" (12–20); the gods answer Enlil: "In Uzumua, the bond of heaven and earth, let us slaughter the Illa-Alla gods; from their blood let us build mankind; the quota of the gods shall be their quota" – to establish the boundary for ever, to put hoe and basket in their hands, to mark out meadow by meadow, keep the dyke straight, make plants flourish, rain (21–41); to establish the boundary, heap grain, [three lines "broken" in the scribe's original], make the field of the Anunnakkū prosper, multiply abundance, perfect the gods' festivals, pour cold water (rev. 1–10); Ullegarra and Annegarra – you shall name their names; ox, sheep, animals, fish and birds, abundance to sprout; En-ul and Nin-ul honoured with pure mouth (11–16); Bēlet-ilī (Sum. Aruru), worthy of lordship, and the gods design great designs: craftsman and fool, sprouting from the earth like barley by themselves – unchangeable as the eternal stars; festivals day and night (17–25); An, Enlil, Ea and Ninmaḫ, the great gods; where mankind was built, Nisaba is established (26–30); colophons.

Sources consulted

  • Rank 1: SEAL 1600 (../../sources/SEAL/KAR-4/node-1600--KAR-4.md), checked line by line against eBL's transliterations of A (../../sources/eBL-fragmentarium/atf/VAT.9307.atf) and B (K.4175.atf).
  • Rank 2: eBL dictionary API (miṣru, īku, palgu, ugāru, karû, qarānu, naqû, kaṣû, isinnu, dešû, ummiānu, banû II and IV, nakāru, urru, šubtu, rabbû, ramānu, kilallān, izuzzu, ṭabāḫu, zakāru, uṣurtu, eṣēru, ešēru, rabû II, šuklulu, mūdû, pirištu, šiāmu, kânu/kunnu, bēlūtu); corpus, Enūma eliš and flood renderings (riksu מוֹסֵרָה, uṣurtu צוּרָה, eṣēru צָר, ṭabāḫu טָבַח, dešû D הִדְשִׁיא, nakāru Dt הוּמַר, isinnu חַג, ḫegallu שֶׁפַע, ummânu אֻמָּן, zunnu גֶּשֶׁם, apālu עָנָה); texts 1–5 (eš₂-gar₃ מִכְסָה, al מַעְדֵּר, dusu סַל, e/pa₅ סוֹלְלָה/תְּעָלָה, a-gar₃ שְׁדֵמָה, Uzumua, Duranki, Nisaba, Ninmaḫ, SIG₇ in text 5); Enūma eliš VI 1–38 and Atra-ḫasīs I (the slain god's blood).
  • Rank 3, after each line's own reading: SEAL's English translation; every departure noted under תרגומים (e.g. 1 "already" not in the Sumerian; 26 "(C the first one)" for saĝ "head(s) = people"; 30 "cherished" for kunnat).
  • Not available: Lambert 2013 (350–360, pl. 65–66), Pettinato 1971 (Das altorientalische Menschenbild, 74ff.), Heidel 1951, Landsberger 1933; no pirate copies were searched for.

Decisions

  1. Bilingual convention as text 6 (Decision 1): the Akkadian line is translated; {שומרית} for the Sumerian-only lines (obv. 1–6, 9a, 39–41; colophon B 1–2); restorations from the parallel half or the other manuscript are named in the apparatus (obv. 7–9: Akkadian names restored from the Sumerian; obv. 9 "great" preserved in B).
  2. Labels obv. N / rev. N (SEAL restarts the numbering on the reverse), obv. 9a (B only), colophon A = SEAL rev. 31–32, colophon B = colophon B 1–10 (our numbering, SEAL's order).
  3. obv. 16–17 (and 19–20): SEAL and B followed against eBL's transliteration of A. SEAL reads A 16 nītepuš, 17 nibni; eBL reads A 16 nīpuš, 17 nītepuš; B has nīpuš / nibni. The Hebrew of 16 is the same either way (מה נַעֲשֶׂה?); 17 = מה נִבְנֶה? with SEAL and B (and with the Sumerian dim₂, which the bilingual tradition renders by banû). B's variants (19 nušbalkit "overturn", 20 nibbi "name") are in the apparatus only.
  4. mīnâ i nīpuš = מה נַעֲשֶׂה? – epēšu = עָשָׂה (corpus) + the Akkadian cohortative: the meaning, not an allusion; tagged [equivalent] ↔ Gen 1:26 (no cognacy). Vocalized in 16 and 19 (identical Akkadian, identical Hebrew).
  5. iškāru (Sum. eš₂-gar₃) = מִכְסָה ("work quota", text 4) – not עָמָל: the brief expected dullu = עָמָל, but dullu does not occur in KAR 4. Never the root עבד.
  6. The slain gods: {d}NAGAR-{d}NAGAR = אִילָּה־אַלָּה (eBL's reading Illa Alla, hyphenated as one pair); SEAL E₁₀?-Illa?, Lambert "Alla", older "Lamga" in the apparatus (open decision 2).
  7. kânu D = כּוֹנֵן (15, 29, 36, 38, rev. 1, 30 מְכוֹנֶנֶת); one deviation by meaning: rev. 16 uktannū with gods as object and "with pure mouth" = "honoured" → הוֹקִירוּ? (CAD kunnu "to treat with honour").
  8. banû II (D bunnû "make beautiful", rev. 20) = לְיַפּוֹת? (as Adapa's banû "beautiful" = יָפֶה), kept apart from banû IV = בָּנָה; the note explains that the Akkadian renders Sum. SIG₇ "sprout" by banû – the equation that bears on text 5 (open decision 2 there) and on obv. 2 here.
  9. SIG₇ in obv. 2 = se₁₂ "to dwell (pl.)", שׁוֹכְנִים? (marû → participle), with SEAL ("lived") and text 5's שָׁכְנוּ?.
  10. Names of the first humans: אוּלֶּגַרָּה and אַנֶּגַרָּה, transliterated; the meanings ("placed for distant time", "whom An placed", both with ĝar "place") in the note. šuma zakāru Gtn = תַּזְכִּיר ותזכיר (corpus šuma zakāru = הִזְכִּיר שֵׁם; not קָרָא, which stays for nabû).
  11. Time: ana ūmī dārûti = לִימֵי נֶצַח (dārû = נֶצַח, text 1), never לְעוֹלָם (reserved for the Gen 3:22 comparison); urra u mūša = יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה.
  12. Scribal note ḫepi (rev. 3–5) = (הסופר כתב:) "שָׁבוּר" – the parentheses mark the added words, the quotation marks the scribe's own word.
  13. Fixed words: uṣurtu = צוּרָה (pl. צוּרוֹת), eṣēru D = צָר (צָרוּ; לָצוּר (צורתן) in 34, so that it is not read "besiege"); riksu = מוֹסֵרָה (EE; קשר = kaṣāru); miṣru = גְּבוּל; īku / palgu = סוֹלְלָה / תְּעָלָה (palgu = פֶּלֶג since the 2026-10-23 harmonization, obv. 13); ugāru = שְׁדֵמָה; eqlu = שָׂדֶה; allu = מַעְדֵּר; tupšikku = סַל; šakānu / ĝar = שָׂם (vocalized); ešēru Št = יִשֵּׁר; karû = כְּרִי [cognate]; qarānu = עָרַם (restored); rabû D = הִרְבָּה; dešû D = הִדְשִׁיא [cognate]; isinnu = חַג; šuklulu = שִׁכְלֵל; naqû = נִסֵּךְ; parakku = דּוּכָן; ṣīru = נַעֲלֶה; šulukat = רָאוּי; šubtu = מוֹשָׁב; būlu = חַיָּה; ummânu = אֻמָּן; nuʾʾû = בּוּר (the Mishnaic word, Avot 2:5; Ps 92:7 has the near-synonym בַּעַר from another root); bēlūtu = אֲדָנוּת; pirištu = סוֹד; niṣirtu = נְצוּרָה [cognate]; mūdû = הַיּוֹדֵעַ; kullumu = הֶרְאָה; apālu = עָנָה; izuzzu = עָמַד; wašābu = יָשַׁב; ina ramāni- = בְּעַצְמָם / מֵעַצְמוֹ.
  14. Names: in a bilingual line the Akkadian name stands in the Hebrew (renderings §1): אָנוּ, אֶנְלִיל, שַׁמַשׁ, אֵאָה, הָאֲנוּנָּכִּי, בֵּלֶת־אִילִי (Sum. אֲרוּרוּ), נִינְמַח, נִיסַבָּה; Sum.-only lines keep the Sumerian forms. אוּזוּמוּאָה (text 4's variant form), אֵן־אוּל, נִין־אוּל, קִידִין־סִין, סוּטֵי, אַשּׁוּר־בָּנִי־אַפְלִי.
  15. Colophon B 7 enūma ilu a[wīlu] rendered as Atra-ḫasīs I 1 (כשהאלים (היו) [אדם]), with ? for the singular spelling; interpreted as the catch-line to the next tablet (our reading of the colophon's structure).
  16. Letter-sequence check of the > lines: no ברא, בראש, שבת, דמות, נשמ, עבד, אדמ, טרם, עדן, לעולם, קרא; נעשה only as the vocalized cohortative נַעֲשֶׂה (16, 19, Decision 4); נִבְנֶה/נִבְנְתָה, צָרוּ, שָׁם ("there", 21) vocalized.

Open decisions for the user

  1. Collate A obv. 16–17 (SEAL nītepuš / nibni vs eBL nīpuš / nītepuš; CDLI photo P282595). The Hebrew of 17 depends on it (מה נִבְנֶה? followed).
  2. The name of the slain gods: אִילָּה־אַלָּה (eBL, followed), הָאַלָּה ("the Alla gods", Lambert; the brief's name) or the older לַמְגָּה.
  3. obv. 11 Sumerian šu gi₄-gi₄ "they repeated" (SEAL) vs eBL's emendation ad!(ŠU) gi₄-gi₄ "they took counsel" – decides whether the text itself has a divine council's "deliberation" (Gen 1:26). The Hebrew follows the Akkadian (ישבו, ובעצמם […]) and is unaffected.
  4. rev. 16 הוֹקִירוּ? (followed, "honoured") or the fixed כּוֹנְנוּ.
  5. rev. 20 לְיַפּוֹת? (SEAL's banû II) or a rendering that shows the translators' equation SIG₇ = banû ("to be built/created"); to be decided together with text 5's open decision 2 and obv. 2 here (שׁוֹכְנִים? vs "sprouting").
  6. obv. 27 מִכְסָה (followed) or עָמָל (the corpus word for the gods' toil, dullu), which would align KAR 4 with Atra-ḫasīs and Enūma eliš but hide the difference of words.
  7. Buy or borrow Lambert 2013 (350–360) and Pettinato 1971: for 1–6, 9a, 10–11, 16–17, 25, 39–41, rev. 2, 11 (the names), 16, 19–21 and the colophon B catch-line.
  8. Print stub and the combined translation.rtl.md are the coordinator's.

Progress log

  • Drafting (2026-10-17): all 84 entries, from SEAL's lines (A, then B, C), each checked against eBL's ATF of A and B; Akkadian normalized and parsed word by word (eBL API); the Sumerian parsed briefly; SEAL's translation read after each line; the distribution of banû (17, 20, 26, rev. 29), epēšu (16, 19), kânu (15, 29, 36, 38, rev. 1, 16, 30), eṣēru/uṣurtu (4, 12, 34, rev. 18, 24–25), šakānu (31, colophon B 6) and ṭabāḫu (25) counted; Enūma eliš VI 33 and Atra-ḫasīs I 204 compared for the blood lines (בדמו בנה את האנושות, אל אחד יטבחו).
  • Review (a) fidelity: obv. 9a הטהור → [הטהור] (the root ku₃ restored by SEAL); obv. 9 [האלים] הגדולים checked (B preserves "great"); brackets of 37, 38, rev. 1, 2, 7, 18–19 set by root; SEAL lemma slips recorded (14 ù lemmatized as ūmu "day"; rev. 17 be-lu-te as bēltu instead of bēlūtu); SEAL's translation departures noted (1, 26, 30).
  • Review (b) consistency: identical Akkadian = identical Hebrew checked as strings: 16 = 19 and 17 = 20 (vocalization made identical: מה נַעֲשֶׂה?, מה נִבְנֶה?), 28 = 35, 29 = 36, 38 = rev. 1, rev. 8 = 23, obv. 32–33 ~ rev. 10, rev. 18 ~ 24–25; renderings against texts 1–6, EE and Atra-ḫasīs (26 = EE VI 33 in the cohortative); four Bible quotations fixed (1 Kgs 22:19 עֹמֵד, a Joshua quotation removed because the checker resolves יהושע as Hosea, the Ezra reference to Asnapar rephrased, a bare לְעוֹלָם rephrased).
  • Review (c) Hebrew: 21 (שם) → (שָׁם) (else read as שָׂם, the šakānu word); 26 בְּדָמָם vocalized; 34 לָצוּר (צורתן); 14 את חדקל ואת פרת – with the object marker for the Hebrew syntax of 14–15; the purpose chain 28–41 and rev. 1–10 kept as infinitive phrases, line by line, without smoothing.
  • Checks: python3 -I verify.py 7 → OK (84 entries; translation = annotated > lines). tools/check_bible_quotes.py on both files → 0 problems. Reserved-word grep: Decision 16.

Not cognate. Here a question ("what?"), answered by other gods (23–26); there a decision.
obv. 17, 20 mīnâ i nibni מה נבנה? נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם (בראשית א:כו) [equivalent] The pair "make … build" (16–17) ↔ נַעֲשֶׂה (א:כו) … וַיִּבְרָא (א:כז). B's 20 nibbi "what shall we name?" joins creating and naming. Rests on SEAL and B against eBL's reading of A (open decision 1).
obv. 23 kilallūšunu Ellil ippalū שניהם ענו לאנליל וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם (בראשית א:כו) [divergence] A dialogue in a council: Enlil asks, the two groups of gods answer; in Gen 1:26 one speaker, no answer.
obv. 26 ina damēšunu i nibnâ amēlūta בדמם נבנה את האנושות נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם (בראשית א:כו) [equivalent] / [divergence] The plural resolution to build man – from the blood of slain gods. Same Hebrew as EE VI 33 (בדמו בנה את האנושות).
rev. 13 alpī immerī būla nūnī u iṣṣūrī שור, צאן, חיה, דגים וציפורים וְיִרְדּוּ בִדְגַת הַיָּם וּבְעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וּבַבְּהֵמָה (בראשית א:כו) [divergence] The same list (cattle, fish, birds) tied to man's creation – man breeds them for the gods; he does not rule them. iṣṣūru (MUŠEN, Sum. mušen) = צִפּוֹר [cognate], where Genesis has עוֹף (harmonization 2026-10-21; was ועופות).
rev. 11 Ullegarra Annegarra אולגרה ואנגרה זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה בָּרָא אֹתָם (בראשית א:כז) [divergence] Two first humans with two names; whether a pair of male and female is not said.
rev. 15 Enul Ninul אן־אול ונין־אול זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה בָּרָא אֹתָם (בראשית א:כז) [equivalent] A lord/lady pair – of primeval gods, not of humans. Weak.
rev. 7 ḫegalla ina māti ana r[ubb]î שפע בארץ [להרבות] פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ וּמִלְאוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ (בראשית א:כח) [cognate] / [divergence] rabû D ~ רבה (restored): man multiplies the land's abundance, not himself.
rev. 23 A isinnī ilī ana šuklulim; B ištu šīmta išīmū חגי האלים לשכלל וַיְכַל אֱלֹהִים בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה (בראשית ב:ב) [divergence] "To complete": man completes the gods' festivals; God completes his work.
rev. 8, 22 isinnī ilī; urra u mūša חגי האלים; יומם ולילה וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אֹתוֹ (בראשית ב:ג) [divergence] Holy time: the gods' rest in Genesis; the gods' festivals as man's task here.
obv. 1, 4, 6 Sum. u₄ … -a-ba ביום אשר בְּיוֹם עֲשׂוֹת יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמָיִם (בראשית ב:ד) [equivalent] "On the day when" opening a creation account (as text 5).
obv. 27 iškar ilī lū iškaršina מכסת האלים – תהי מכסתן וְאָדָם אַיִן לַעֲבֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה (בראשית ב:ה) [divergence] Man is created to work – as in Gen 2:5 – but the work is the gods' quota, for the gods.
obv. 41 Sum. {im}šeĝ₃ {im}šeĝ₃ גשם, גשם כִּי לֹא הִמְטִיר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים עַל הָאָרֶץ וְאָדָם אַיִן לַעֲבֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה (בראשית ב:ה) [equivalent] Rain and the worker side by side, in the list of man's tasks; Gen 2:5 lacks both. Sumerian only. Our proposal.
obv. 39; rev. 6 Sum. u₂ ḫi-a; eqel Anunnakī צמחים שונים; שדה האנונכי וְכָל עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה טֶרֶם יִצְמָח (בראשית ב:ה) [divergence] Plants and fields as the work of man – on the field of the gods.
obv. 5, 13, 37 īka u palga; īka ana šutēšuri סוללה ופלג (13; 5, from the Sumerian: סוללה ותעלה); סוללה [ליישר] וְאֵד יַעֲלֶה מִן הָאָרֶץ וְהִשְׁקָה אֶת כָּל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה (בראשית ב:ו) [divergence] Irrigation by dykes and canals, kept by man; in Gen 2:6 water rises by itself.
obv. 25–26 Illa-Alla i niṭbuḫa; ina damēšunu את אילה־אלה נטבחה; בדמם וַיִּיצֶר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם עָפָר מִן הָאֲדָמָה (בראשית ב:ז) [divergence] Blood alone, from slain gods – no clay (unlike Atra-ḫasīs I), no dust, no guilt (unlike EE VI's Qingu). ṭabāḫu = טבח [cognate].
obv. 26 (Sum.); rev. 20 mu₂-mu₂-e-de₃; kīma šeʾim ana ramānišu ana bunnî (Sum. ki-ta sig₇) (בשומרית: להצמיח); כשעורה, מעצמו, ליפות? וַיִּיצֶר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם עָפָר מִן הָאֲדָמָה (בראשית ב:ז) [divergence] In the Sumerian, mankind "grows" from the blood and sprouts from the earth "like barley, by themselves" (as in the Song of the Hoe).
obv. 4, 12; rev. 18, 24–25 uṣurāt šamê u erṣeti; uṣurāte … uṣṣirū צורות השמים והארץ; צורות … צרו וַיִּיצֶר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם (בראשית ב:ז) [cognate] eṣēru/uṣurtu ~ יצר: the gods "form forms" – the designs of the world and of mankind; Genesis's verb of man's forming.
— — — וַיִּפַּח בְּאַפָּיו נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים (בראשית ב:ז) [absent] No breath.
obv. 24 ina Uzumua rikis šamê u erṣeti באוזומואה, מוסרת השמים והארץ וַיִּטַּע יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים גַּן בְּעֵדֶן מִקֶּדֶם; וַיָּשֶׂם שָׁם אֶת הָאָדָם (בראשית ב:ח) [divergence] A named place of man's creation – "where flesh grew", the bond of heaven and earth at Nippur; not a garden.
rev. 11 Ul-le-ĝar-ra An-ne₂-ĝar-ra אולגרה ואנגרה וַיָּשֶׂם שָׁם אֶת הָאָדָם (בראשית ב:ח) [equivalent] Both names contain Sum. ĝar "to place": "placed for distant time", "whom An placed". Our proposal.
obv. 30–31 alla u tupšikka ana qātīšina ana šakāni מעדר וסל בידיהן לשׂום וַיָּשֶׂם שָׁם אֶת הָאָדָם (בראשית ב:ח) [divergence] שׂים: God puts man in the garden; the gods put the tools in man's hands.
obv. 6, 14 Idiqlat u Puratta חדקל ופרת וְשֵׁם הַנָּהָר הַשְּׁלִישִׁי חִדֶּקֶל … וְהַנָּהָר הָרְבִיעִי הוּא פְרָת (בראשית ב:יד) [cognate] The rivers' banks are "set" before man is made.
obv. 27–29 iškāru; miṣra ana kunni מכסה; גבול לכונן וַיַּנִּחֵהוּ בְגַן עֵדֶן לְעָבְדָהּ וּלְשָׁמְרָהּ (בראשית ב:טו) [divergence] Work and keeping: here the boundary-keeping of fields and canals "for days of eternity".
obv. 30 alla u tupšikka מעדר וסל בְּזֵעַת אַפֶּיךָ תֹּאכַל לֶחֶם (בראשית ג:יט) [divergence] The tools are given at creation; in Genesis hard labour comes after the expulsion.
rev. 20 kīma šeʾim … (Sum. ki-ta) כשעורה, מעצמו עַד שׁוּבְךָ אֶל הָאֲדָמָה כִּי מִמֶּנָּה לֻקָּחְתָּ (בראשית ג:יט) [divergence] Man comes from the earth like grain (Sumerian).
rev. 17 Bēlet-ilī (Sum. Aruru) בלת־אילי כִּי הִוא הָיְתָה אֵם כָּל חָי (בראשית ג:כ) [equivalent] The mother goddess "worthy of lordship" designs mankind with the gods.
rev. 12 šumēšunu tazzanakkar את שמותם תזכיר ותזכיר וַיִּקְרָא הָאָדָם שֵׁם אִשְׁתּוֹ חַוָּה (בראשית ג:כ) [divergence] The verb is zakāru "to pronounce, remember" (Gtn, "keep naming"), not nabû: names to be recited, not only given.
obv. 11, 16 the gods' council ישבו, ובעצמם; מה נעשה? הֵן הָאָדָם הָיָה כְּאַחַד מִמֶּנּוּ (בראשית ג:כב) [equivalent] Divine plural.
obv. 28, 35 ana ūmī dārûti לימי נצח וְאָכַל וָחַי לְעֹלָם (בראשית ג:כב) [divergence] "Eternity" belongs to man's labour ("for days of eternity"), not to his life.
obv. 30 alla u tupšikka מעדר וסל לַעֲבֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר לֻקַּח מִשָּׁם (בראשית ג:כג) [divergence]
rev. 29–30 ašar amēlūtu ibbanû Nisaba … kunnat במקום אשר האנושות נבנתה, ניסבה … מכוננת וַיַּשְׁכֵּן מִקֶּדֶם לְגַן עֵדֶן אֶת הַכְּרֻבִים (בראשית ג:כד) [divergence] A divine figure established at the place of man's creation: the grain goddess (abundance), not guardians of a lost garden. Weak; our proposal.
rev. 11–12; obv. 20 (B) Ullegarra Annegarra … šumēšunu tazzanakkar; B mīnâ i nibbi אולגרה ואנגרה – את שמותם תזכיר ותזכיר וַיִּקְרָא אֶת שְׁמָם אָדָם בְּיוֹם הִבָּרְאָם (בראשית ה:ב) [equivalent] The first humans receive names at their creation; two names here, one (אָדָם) there.
rev. 22 urra u mūša יומם ולילה וְיוֹם וָלַיְלָה לֹא יִשְׁבֹּתוּ (בראשית ח:כב) [equivalent] The unceasing cycle – here of the gods' festivals.
obv. 26 damu דם שֹׁפֵךְ דַּם הָאָדָם בָּאָדָם דָּמוֹ יִשָּׁפֵךְ: כִּי בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם (בראשית ט:ו) [divergence] Blood and the divine: here gods' blood is the stuff of man; there man's divine image forbids shedding his blood.
obv. 16–17, 25–26 i nīpuš, i nibni, i niṭbuḫa, i nibnâ נעשה, נבנה, נטבחה, נבנה הָבָה נִבְנֶה לָּנוּ עִיר (בראשית יא:ד); הָבָה נֵרְדָה וְנָבְלָה שָׁם שְׂפָתָם (בראשית יא:ז) [cognate] / [equivalent] Chains of cohortatives; banû = בנה with the same form (נִבְנֶה).
rev. 21 kakkab šamê dārûti כוכבי השמים הנצחיים כְּכוֹכְבֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם (בראשית כב:יז) [divergence] Stars as an image of permanence here, of multitude there.
rev. 2 karû כרי וְרֹב דָּגָן וְתִירֹשׁ (בראשית כז:כח) [equivalent] Grain heaps; karû = Mishnaic כְּרִי [cognate].
obv. 34 ugāru ana ugāri ana uṣṣuri שדמה לשדמה – לצור וַיָּצַר אֹתוֹ בַּחֶרֶט (שמות לב:ד) [cognate] eṣēru = צור/יצר "to form, draw".
rev. 19 ummânu ana ummâni nuʾʾû ana nuʾʾî אמן לאמן, בור לבור מִי שָׂם פֶּה לָאָדָם אוֹ מִי יָשׂוּם אִלֵּם אוֹ חֵרֵשׁ אוֹ פִקֵּחַ אוֹ עִוֵּר (שמות ד:יא) [equivalent] The kinds of men (skilled and fool) are designed by the gods; cf. text 3.
obv. 26 damu דם כִּי נֶפֶשׁ הַבָּשָׂר בַּדָּם הִוא (ויקרא יז:יא) [cognate]
obv. 29 miṣru גבול לֹא תַסִּיג גְּבוּל רֵעֲךָ אֲשֶׁר גָּבְלוּ רִאשֹׁנִים (דברים יט:יד) [equivalent] Field boundaries "for ever".
rev. 31 pirištu … mūdû mūdâ likallim סוד: היודע את היודע יראה הַנִּסְתָּרֹת לַיהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ; וְהַנִּגְלֹת לָנוּ וּלְבָנֵינוּ (דברים כט:כח) [divergence] The account of man's creation is a "secret" for the initiated; Genesis tells it to all.
obv. 21 ilū rabûtu šūt izzizū האלים הגדולים אשר עמדו (שם) רָאִיתִי אֶת יְהוָה יֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסְאוֹ וְכָל צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם עֹמֵד עָלָיו (מלכים א כב:יט) [equivalent] The council standing before the throne. Our proposal.
obv. 3, 15 Sum. ki du₃, ki ĝar; ukinnū הארץ נבנתה; לשׂום את הארץ; כוננו יֹצֵר הָאָרֶץ וְעֹשָׂהּ הוּא כוֹנְנָהּ לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ לָשֶׁבֶת יְצָרָהּ (ישעיהו מה:יח) [equivalent] Earth "built", "placed", "made firm" – and for dwelling.
colophon B 5 niṣirtu נצורת וּנְצֻרוֹת וְלֹא יְדַעְתָּם (ישעיהו מח:ו) [cognate] Hidden things.
rev. 21 ša lā uttakkaru kakkab šamê אשר לא יומר – כוכבי השמים נֹתֵן שֶׁמֶשׁ לְאוֹר יוֹמָם חֻקֹּת יָרֵחַ וְכוֹכָבִים לְאוֹר לָיְלָה (ירמיהו לא:לד) [equivalent] The unchangeable order of the stars as guarantee of a human order (Jer 31:34–35). Our proposal.
obv. 4, 12; rev. 18 uṣurāt צורות צוּרַת הַבַּיִת וּתְכוּנָתוֹ … וְכָל צוּרֹתָו (יחזקאל מג:יא) [cognate] "Forms" = the design of a building.
obv. 29 miṣra ana kunni גבול לכונן גְּבוּל-שַׂמְתָּ בַּל-יַעֲבֹרוּן (תהלים קד:ט) [equivalent] God sets the boundary of the waters; here man keeps the boundaries for ever.
obv. 30 tupšikku סל כַּפָּיו מִדּוּד תַּעֲבֹרְנָה (תהלים פא:ז) [equivalent] The basket of servitude.
rev. 9 mê kaṣûti ana naqê מים קרים לנסך וַיִּשְׁאֲבוּ מַיִם וַיִּשְׁפְּכוּ לִפְנֵי יְהוָה (שמואל א ז:ו) [equivalent] Water libation. Weak.

Proposals for the shared renderings

  1. Corpus §2/§3: iškāru / Sum. eš₂-gar₃ = מִכְסָה, next to dullu = עָמָל and šupšikku/tupšikku = סַל; allu = מַעְדֵּר (Akkadian, as Sum. al).
  2. epēšu cohortative = נַעֲשֶׂה (always vocalized), tagged ↔ Gen 1:26; and the stative נַעֲשָׂה vocalized (text 6).
  3. banû II (be beautiful; D bunnû) = יָפֶה / יִפָּה, kept apart from banû IV = בָּנָה; record the scholarly equation SIG₇ = banû (KAR 4 rev. 20) in the corpus file, for text 5's open decision 2.
  4. miṣru = גְּבוּל; ana ūmī dārûti = לִימֵי נֶצַח; urra u mūša = יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה.
  5. karû = כְּרִי [cognate] and niṣirtu = נְצוּרָה [cognate] for guidelines §6.7.
  6. šuma zakāru Gtn = doubled verb תַּזְכִּיר ותזכיר (as Adapa's ṣiāḫu Gtn).
  7. Names (§1): אִילָּה־אַלָּה (open decision 2), אוּלֶּגַרָּה, אַנֶּגַרָּה, אֵן־אוּל, נִין־אוּל; Uzumua אוּזוּמוּאָה confirmed for KAR 4.

Lessons for the guidelines

  • Compare the two digital transliterations of the key verbs: SEAL and eBL disagree on A obv. 16–17 – exactly the "what shall we make? what shall we build?" lines; a third witness (B) and the Sumerian decided provisionally. Record such disagreements as open decisions (collation by photo).
  • SEAL lemma slips again (obv. 14 ù = ūmu "day"; rev. 17 bēltu for bēlūti; obv. 21 B rabîš for GAL{meš}): parse the form.
  • Colophons carry catch-lines that link texts: KAR 4 B ends with enūma ilu a[wīlu], the incipit of Atra-ḫasīs – a Nineveh compilation put the creation of man from slain gods' blood immediately before the Atra-ḫasīs epic. Read colophons as data for the corpus, not as appendices.
  • School copies: a syllable-alphabet column beside a literary text (A, B) means the text was a school exercise; eBL then catalogues the tablet as a "list" – search eBL by transliteration, not only by genre.
  • check_bible_quotes.py bug: the book key drops י and ו, so יהושע resolves to הושע (Hosea); a reference like ד:י after any backticked word is checked as Genesis. Tool fix needed (or quote Joshua elsewhere).

Harmonization by the coordinator

  • Spelling: שמים (texts 3–4 had שמיים), תהילה (text 2 had תהלה).
  • Checked across all seven texts: no אדמה, טרם, עולם or root עבד in any Hebrew line (the cross-text rules of ../renderings.md §5).
  • Known small inconsistency left for the user: Sum. numun₂ is אַסְפֶּסֶת? in text 3 (43) and חַלְפָה in text 4.
  • tools/check_bible_quotes.py fixed: the book key dropped the matres, so יהושע resolved as הושע (found by the text 6–7 translator).
  • 2026-10-21, cross-corpus harmonization (the lead's decisions on STATUS.md §6; corpus renderings.md §8): mušen = צִפּוֹר – Enki and Ninḫursaĝa 18 עוף השמים … אינו אוכל → ציפור השמים … אינה אוכלת (note: Ps 8:9 צִפּוֹר שָׁמַיִם), the Song of the Hoe 83 עוף האל הוא → ציפור האל היא, KAR 4 rev. 13 ועופות → וציפורים (iṣṣūru = MUŠEN, [cognate]); the Hoe 12 got the first-occurrence [equivalent] note on סַפִּיר (Exod 24:10, Ezek 1:26, Job 28:6); Inana אִינַנָּה also in the apparatus and the Hoe heading 49–51 (was אינאנה); Eridu rev. 19′ note on tu₆ / tû; Eridu open decision 7 settled. Already in line: סַפִּיר, פּוּךְ (E&Nḫ 230), וְזִיר, הַ־מֶה, כְּרִי.

Open decisions for the user (the most important; details in each text's section)

Sources to buy or borrow: Izre'el 2001 (Adapa), Attinger 1984 (Enki and Ninḫursaĝa), Ceccarelli 2016 / Klein 1997 (Enki and Ninmaḫ, incl. the bilingual), Farber 1997 (Hoe), Alster & Vanstiphout 1987 (Grain and Sheep), Lambert 2013 (Founding of Eridu and KAR 4; also Enūma eliš), Ambos 2004, Pettinato 1971. Lambert 2013 alone would cover texts 6–7 and check project 1.
  2. Enki and Ninḫursaĝa 220: "swore an oath" (followed: nam-erim₂ kud) or the traditional "cursed".
  3. Grain and Sheep 27, 39: grain and sheep "dwelt" with the gods (ETCSL's lemma, followed) or were "created" (ETCSL's translation); KAR 4 rev. 20 (SIG₇ = banû) bears on it.
  4. Enki and Ninmaḫ: add the biblical disability word in parentheses ((= עִוֵּר)) or keep the Sumerian description only (followed); tiru אִישׁ־חָצֵר or סָרִיס.
  5. Adapa MB 75′: "you shall not live!" as a statement (followed) or Foster's question; MB 15′ and 58′ readings.
  6. Song of the Hoe: Uzuea (edition, followed) or the familiar Uzumua in the lines; ki הארץ (followed) or קרקע.
  7. KAR 4: the slain gods' name (Illa-Alla, followed; Alla; Lamga); obv. 11 "repeated" (SEAL) or "took counsel" (eBL emendation: decides whether the text has a deliberating council); obv. 16–17 to be collated on the photo.
  8. Corpus-wide: ṭeḫû (נִגַּשׁ here, קָרַב in Enūma eliš); šipru (פֹּעַל / מְלָאכָה, project 1); the {שומרית} tag for Sumerian-only lines of bilinguals.
